dossier.public_summary: The 12-day dip alternates between a deep eclipse and a shallow one with a strong odd-even difference, and the individual transits do not agree with each other. The depth also changes dramatically between sectors and between the same pipeline. Together this is the pattern of an eclipsing binary seen at twice its period, not a consistent planet transit.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ strongly (depth_odd_ppm 246.9 vs depth_even_ppm 1015, depth_difference 0.7567, depth_ratio 4.1) with 6.293 sigma and red_noise 1.202, a classic signature of a binary folded at half the observed period. The sector-level odd/even check shows same sign across sectors.

Individual transit depths are inconsistent (chi2 48.32811760573582 dof 4, p_consistent 8.062380542378944e-10). Top 3 transits carry share_of_top_3 0.947 of the signal and outlier epoch 1 at 63 ppm (mean_depth_ppm 713) is non-detection, so the 12-d period dip is not seen consistently.

Depth truly changes: p_constant_all 3.356148950282928e-08, SPOC 2-min p_constant 0.00017985181732128498 with depth_ppm 309 err_ppm 93 versus TESS-SPOC depth_ppm 913 err 96, and per-sector depths 805 ppm, 63 ppm, 913 ppm. This is not a calibration offset.
